title: Rollout guardrails + automated rollback policy for KV compaction/eviction (runtime-1.22)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Context
KV cache compaction + tier-aware eviction is a runtime change that can materially affect tail latency under burst + mixed-length workloads. We need explicit guardrails for staged rollout (internal canary → Hosted subset → Dedicated pools) with (1) KPIs that block progression, (2) automated rollback triggers that are safe and fast, and (3) comms templates for incidents/escalations.

This ticket defines rollout policy requirements (PM-owned) that Release Eng + SRE + Runtime will implement in rollout tooling / playbooks.

Scope
- Define stage gates (what metrics must be green to expand from 0% → canary → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%).
- Define automated rollback criteria (what metrics trigger rollback, evaluation windows, and what “rollback” means operationally).
- Define comms templates (Slack + Support + customer-facing) to minimize confusion during canary incidents.

Out of scope
- Implementing dashboards/alerts (covered in ENG-4830 / SRE work) beyond specifying required signals.
- Customer-facing Console UI (initial release uses config/flags).

Owners / stakeholders
- PM rollout policy: Paula Mendes (assignee), Marissa Cole (creator)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Runtime: Omar El-Sayed, Sofia Ivanova
- Release train: Connor O’Brien

Rollout stages (required)
Stage 0: Internal shadow + perf canary validation
- Compaction enabled only in internal perf canary + staging clusters.
- Gate: perf canary scenario “mixed-length bursts” must pass for 3 consecutive runs (no regression beyond thresholds below).

Stage 1: Internal production canary (employee traffic / low-risk tenants)
- 0.5–1% of Hosted traffic in 1 region; exclude top enterprise tenants.
- Duration: minimum 24 hours.
- Gate: no automated rollback events; all blocking KPIs green.

Stage 2: Hosted subset
- 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% per region.
- Minimum dwell time per step: 6 hours (business hours) + 12 hours overnight for at least one step.
- Gate per step: blocking KPIs green; SRE sign-off required for >25%.

Stage 3: Dedicated pools
- Opt-in by pool (start with 1 low-risk pool), then expand by tier.
- Explicit exception: Dedicated can be held at lower default compaction budget until Hosted is 100% in at least 2 regions.

Blocking KPIs (must be green to proceed)
All thresholds below are relative to baseline (control cohort without compaction/eviction) unless noted.

A) Tail latency
- p99 end-to-end latency (decode-heavy routes) regression: > +8% over 30-minute window blocks progression.
- p95 end-to-end latency regression: > +5% over 30-minute window blocks progression.
- “Spike detector”: any single 5-minute bucket with p99 > +20% triggers investigation; two buckets within 60 minutes triggers rollback (see rollback rules).

B) Errors / stability
- 5xx rate regression: > +0.05 percentage points over 30-minute window blocks.
- Request shedding / overload rejections regression: > +0.10 percentage points over 30-minute window blocks.
- GPU OOM events: any increase > 0 (new OOMs) during rollout step triggers immediate rollback for that region/pool.

C) Compaction/eviction health (new runtime signals)
- Compaction time budget overrun rate: > 1% of intervals over 30 minutes blocks.
- Bytes moved per request (p95) “sanity”: if > 2× baseline for 30 minutes, block + investigate.
- Eviction rate: if eviction_count/request exceeds 2× baseline AND correlated with latency regression (p99 +8%), triggers rollback.

D) Correctness guardrails
- Any detected correctness incident (allocator invariant violation, data corruption signal, repeated “relocation failed” errors) triggers immediate rollback and incident declaration.

Automated rollback policy (requirements)
Definition of rollback
- Rollback = disable compaction + eviction feature flags for the rollout cohort (region/pool) via rollout controller + config propagation.
- If “disable” fails to propagate within 10 minutes (config propagation delay / control-plane issue), oncall must use emergency kill-switch path (runtime config override) per runbook.

Rollback triggers (automated)
- Immediate rollback (no human approval required):
  1) Any new GPU OOM event in cohort while feature is enabled (single event).
  2) Correctness signals (allocator invariant violations; repeated relocation failures > 3/min for 5 min).
  3) p99 regression > +15% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Fast rollback (pager + auto-rollback after 5-minute grace unless oncall cancels):
  1) p99 regression > +8% sustained for 30 minutes.
  2) 5xx regression > +0.05pp sustained for 30 minutes.
  3) Two 5-minute buckets within 60 minutes where p99 > +20%.

Evaluation windows / anti-flap rules
- Use 10-minute and 30-minute rolling windows; rollback only if threshold is met for 2 of the last 3 evaluation intervals (to avoid noisy single samples), except Immediate rollback triggers.
- Cooldown: after rollback, cohort remains disabled for minimum 24 hours; re-enable requires runtime + SRE approval and a documented change (e.g., reduced compaction budget, higher fragmentation trigger, or bugfix PR landed).

What blocks “progress to next step” vs “rollback current step”
- Blocking KPIs prevent increasing rollout percentage but do not necessarily disable feature.
- Rollback triggers always disable feature for cohort.
- If blocked for > 8 hours without a clear remediation plan, default action is rollback (PM policy to reduce prolonged risk exposure).

Manual override / authority
- Who can pause rollout: SRE oncall, Release train lead (Connor O’Brien), Runtime TL (Omar El-Sayed).
- Who can override an automated rollback (rare): SRE oncall only, and must leave an audit note in #incidents thread + Linear comment explaining why metrics are believed to be false positive.

Required comms templates
1) Internal Slack (rollout channel) — “pause”
Template:
“PAUSING runtime-1.22 KV compaction rollout in <region/pool>. Trigger: <metric> exceeded threshold (<value> vs <baseline>). Action: rollout paused at <percent> and cohort held. Owners: SRE <name>, Runtime <name>. Next update in 30 minutes.”

2) Internal Slack (incident channel) — “rollback executed”
Template:
“ROLLBACK executed for KV compaction in <region/pool>. Reason: <trigger>. Time to disable: <X min>. Current status: <p99 delta>, <5xx>, <OOM count>. Next steps: capture traces (compaction spans), allocator snapshot, and open follow-up ticket(s).”

3) Support macro (for customer ticket)
Template:
“We identified elevated tail latency under burst conditions in <region> associated with a runtime change under staged rollout. We have disabled the feature for your cohort and are monitoring. Next update by <time>. If you can share request IDs / timestamps for spikes, we’ll correlate with traces and allocator metrics.”

4) Customer email (enterprise escalation)
Template:
Subject: Update: Mitigation applied for tail-latency spikes in <region>
Body:
“During a staged runtime rollout, we observed elevated p99 latency for a subset of traffic in <region>. We rolled back the change for your cohort at <time> and latency has returned to baseline. We’re investigating root cause (KV cache memory management under bursty mixed-length workloads) and will provide a follow-up with preventative steps and a revised rollout plan. No action needed on your side; if you have any timestamps or request IDs, please share to assist correlation.”

5) Status page guidance
- External status page update only if impact crosses customer-defined threshold (e.g., sustained p99 regression with errors for > 15 minutes affecting multiple tenants). Otherwise, handle via targeted comms/support.

Acceptance criteria
- SRE + Release Eng confirm the above gates and rollback triggers can be represented in rollout controller (or documented as manual where automation not possible).
- Runtime confirms signals exist or will exist for: p95/p99 deltas by cohort, OOM count by cohort, compaction budget overrun rate, eviction rate, relocation failure signals.
- Runbook updated to reference this policy (link from runbook back to this ticket).

Links
- Release train coordination: ENG-4829
- Kill-switch/config plumbing: ENG-4826
- Metrics ticket: ENG-4822
- Perf canary scenario: ENG-4828
- Dashboard panels: ENG-4830
- Customer impact messaging: PM-611

Notes
- Dedicated pools: allow stricter rollback criteria around OOM and request shedding due to higher sensitivity to burst traffic patterns.
- If compaction is rolled back for a region, do not re-enable until a post-rollback note is posted with (a) suspected cause, (b) proposed config change or patch, (c) validation plan (bench + canary).
comments: 2026-01-14 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on immediate rollback for any new OOM. For tail latency, propose we use relative deltas vs control cohort (same region) to avoid regional drift. Also need anti-flap logic; otherwise we’ll churn flags during load transitions.

2026-01-16 (Omar El-Sayed): We can emit “compaction_budget_overrun_total” and “relocation_failed_total” counters. Eviction rate will exist once tier-aware eviction lands. For early canary, if eviction isn’t enabled yet, the eviction clauses should be gated on feature flag state.
2026-01-18 (Connor O’Brien): Rollout controller supports step gates + auto rollback on alert conditions, but we need precise alert definitions. Please specify windows and ‘2 of last 3’ logic (added).
2026-01-26 (Marissa Cole): After the brief canary spike last week, we should treat “two 5-min p99 > +20% buckets within 60m” as rollback. This catches burst-driven spikes without waiting 30 minutes.

2026-02-03 (Paula Mendes): Added comms templates for Support + enterprise escalation. Support asked that we include ‘no action required’ + request IDs for correlation. Also added cooldown policy (24h) to reduce re-enable churn.
2026-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): Final policy looks good. Request: clearly define authority to override auto rollback (SRE oncall only) and require audit note. Approved.
2026-02-18 (Paula Mendes): Marking Done. Policy shared with #eng-releases and linked from runtime compaction runbook draft.
